messages.subject: question about the garchFit
messages.body_plain:
Good afternoon professor Diethelm Wuertz 
 
My name is Daniel Parra, I'm economist and I'm studying time series
models for financial variables. I'm working in R with their package
(fGarch), which I found very interesting and useful.
 
I would ask you please help me with the following question.
 
How do I do to estimate a ARMA(6,1)-GARCH(1,1) without the coefficients
AR(1), AR(2), AR(3), AR(4) and AR(5)?
 
For example, I've tried in this way,
 
y = garchFit(~arma(6,1)+garch(1,1), r.IGBC, trace=F,cond.dist = "dnorm")
 
and result is:
 
Coefficient(s):
Mu       0.20950912  
ar1       -0.27087286   
ar2       0.06539889  
ar3       -0.08086325     I don't want estimate these coefficients
ar4       0.00391767   
ar5        0.05273713  
ar6       -0.04344611   
ma1     0.49958456   
omega  0.44834015   
alpha1  0.34024705   
beta1    0.46750871  
 
According to the results above, you can see that the routine estimate
the coefficients AR (1) to AR (5), which I don't want in the model. How
do I restrict them on the code?.

messages.subject: dmvsnorm & mvst in fMultivar
messages.body_plain:
>>>> "AA" == Adelchi Azzalini <azzalini at stat.unipd.it>
>>>> on Tue, 26 Aug 2008 10:44:16 +0200

   AA> Dear Colleagues,
   AA> 
   AA> I am writing about some functions incorporated into your package
   AA> "fMultivar", specifically dmvsnorm & mvst, which originate from 
   AA> packages 'sn'. In principle, it is welcome that your package
   AA> incorporates some routines from my package. Unfortunately, this
   AA> operation has been done improperly, and the effect is seriously
   AA> misleading for the user.
   AA> 
   AA> In the documentation of the above-mentioned functions, one reads:
   AA> 
   AA> mu, Omega, alpha, df: [*mvsnorm][*mvst] - 
   AA>            the model parameters: 
   AA>            'mu' a vector of mean values, one for each column, 
   AA>            'Omega' the covariance matrix, 
   AA>            'alpha' the skewness vector, and 
   AA>            'df' the number of degrees of freedom which is a measure for
   AA>           the fatness of the tails (excess kurtosis). 
   AA> 
   AA> and in the code mu is set equal to xi, which is a location parameter,
   AA> but _not_ the mean, as the documentation wrongly indicates. In fact 
   AA> in the skew-t case the mean may even not exist. Similarly, Omega is 
   AA> described as "the covariance matrix", which suggests that this is
   AA> the covariance matrix of the distribution, but it is not true.
   AA> Omega is _a_ covariance matrix, which is related to the covariance
   AA> matrix (when this one exists) but it is different. For the
   AA> parametrization based on mean and variance, see later.
   AA> 
   AA> In addition, in the code of dmvsnorm, for the one-dimensional case
   AA> there is the assignment
   AA> 
   AA>  ans = dsn(x, location = xi[1], scale = as.vector(Omega)[1], 
   AA>            shape = alpha[1])
   AA> 
   AA> which is wrong since in this case the scale is the square root of
   AA> Omega. Similar errors exist in pmvsnorm, dmvst, pmvst.
   AA> 
   AA> Please note that the above remarks do not attempt to be exhaustive,
   AA> since I have not done a full scan of your code and documentation.
   AA> These are just the problems which I have spotted after a quick
   AA> browsing of your package.
   AA> 
   AA> I take this opportunity to draw your attention to this note:
   AA>    http://tango.stat.unipd.it/SN/announce2.html
   AA> When the new "version 1.xx" will be available, it will include
   AA> a parametrization based on mean/variance.
   AA> 
   AA> With best wishes,
   AA> 
   AA> Adelchi Azzalini

Dear Adelchi,

Thank you for your message. Your comment is very helpful for us because we
are in the process to clean some packages and hopefully we will fix the
issues you raised.

Best regards,
Yohan

-- 
PhD student
Swiss Federal Institute of Technology
Zurich

messages.subject: fMultivar functions not loading under R-2.7
messages.subject_clean: fMultivar functions not loading under R-2.7
messages.body_plain:
I've been using R-2.4 with Rmetrics successfuly for a year or two.

I recently moved to Ubuntu Linux 8.04, loaded R via apt-get install R-base
etc. etc...

then in the R interface i ran install.packages("fMultivar"), chose the CRAN
mirror and it loaded fMultivar and all the required dependecies.

However, when I try to run the same code which makes use of the indicator
calculators (emaTA etc.) I get this warning:

Error: could not find function "fMultivar.emaTA"

upon further inspection looking at the available functions for fMultivar

> listFunctions(fMultivar)
 [1] "contour.gridData"     "dcauchy2d"            "delliptical2d"
 [4] ".delliptical2dSlider" "density2d"            "dmvsnorm"
 [7] "dmvst"                "dnorm2d"              ".dnorm2d"
[10] "dt2d"                 ".First.lib"           ".gfunc2d"
[13] "grid2d"               "gridData"             "hexBinning"
[16] "hist2d"               "integrate2d"          "mvFit"
[19] ".mvsnormFit"          ".mvsnormPlot"         ".mvsnorm.plot.1"
[22] ".mvsnorm.plot.1A"     ".mvsnorm.plot.1B"     ".mvsnorm.plot.2"
[25] ".mvsnorm.plot.3"      ".mvsnorm.plot.4"      ".mvsnorm.plot.5"
[28] ".mvstFit"             ".mvstPlot"            ".mvst.plot.1"
[31] ".mvst.plot.1A"        ".mvst.plot.1B"        ".mvst.plot.2"
[34] ".mvst.plot.3"         ".mvst.plot.4"         ".mvst.plot.5"
[37] "pcauchy2d"            "persp.gridData"       "plot.fMV"
[40] "plot.hexBinning"      "plot.squareBinning"   "pmvsnorm"
[43] "pmvst"                "pnorm2d"              ".pnorm2d"
[46] "pt2d"                 "rcauchy2d"            "rmvsnorm"
[49] "rmvst"                "rnorm2d"              ".rnorm2d"
[52] "rt2d"                 "show.fMV"             "squareBinning"
[55] "summary.fMV"          ".TInt"                ".TOwen"

shows that none of the indicators previously available under R-2.4 are
available.

Is this just a setting somehere in R that I need to enable?  In Linux
maybe?  Do I need to update the packages maybe?  I'm using fMultivar version
260.72.

Thanks in advance
Theo
-- 
Theodore Van Rooy
http://greentheo.scroggles.com
